nodes.title: Semistable vertex sets, semistable decompositions and the skeleton of a curve
nodes.statement: Standing conventions of the source (Section 3 opening): K is algebraically closed and complete with respect to a nontrivial nonarchimedean valuation; X is a smooth connected algebraic curve over K, X̂ is its smooth completion (a curve, not an analytification) and D = X̂ ∖ X is the finite set of punctures. Analytifications are written X^an and X̂^an. A semistable vertex set of X̂ is a finite set V of type-2 points such that X̂^an ∖ V is a disjoint union of open balls and finitely many open annuli; a semistable vertex set of X additionally has the punctures in distinct open-ball components. The skeleton Σ(X, V) = V ∪ ⋃ Σ(A) over the generalized open annuli A of the decomposition; the completed skeleton Σ̂(X, V) is its closure in X̂^an, equal to Σ(X, V) ∪ D, a graph with vertex set V ∪ D whose open edges are the skeleta of the annuli. (Lemma 3.2) The limit boundary of an open ball component is a single vertex; an open annulus component S(a)^+ has σ: (0, r) → A (r = val(a)) extending continuously to [0, r] with endpoints in V (possibly equal); a punctured ball has endpoints one vertex and one puncture. (Lemma 3.4) Σ is closed, compact iff X = X̂; its limit boundary is D; the components of X^an ∖ Σ are open balls with one-point limit boundary in Σ; Σ is the set of points with no affinoid neighbourhood isomorphic to B(1) and disjoint from V.
hypotheses: K algebraically closed and complete with respect to a nontrivial nonarchimedean valuation (the paper's standing assumption); type-2 points; annuli are standard generalized open annuli S(a)^+ with modulus val(a).
Semistable vertex sets of X̂ correspond bijectively to isomorphism classes of semistable formal models (Theorem 4.11, not read).
proofSteps: Lemma 3.2(1): for an open ball A ≅ B(1)^+ define ||f|| = lim_{r→0} ||f||_r for f regular on an affine open containing A (piecewise affine in r with finitely many slope changes by Proposition 2.10); this is a multiplicative norm defining a point x, and the extension of B(1)^+ ∪ {Shilov point} → X^an is continuous by checking neighbourhoods of the Shilov point along an annulus S(a)^+ where f has no zeros (Lemma 2.13); compactness gives closedness of A ∪ {x}.
Lemma 3.4: (1)-(3) follow from Lemma 3.2 and Lemma 2.12 (an annulus minus its skeleton is a union of open balls); (4) uses Proposition 2.4 (skeleton of an annulus).
acceptance: Reviewer-authored test: for a curve with good reduction the single Gauss-type point of the reduction is a semistable vertex set with Σ = V. The statement that its vertex genus is the genus of the curve uses the genus theory of BPR14 Section 4, which was not read.

For an elliptic curve with bad reduction the minimal skeleton is a loop of length −val(j). The tropicalization paper states this in its introduction, citing [BPR13, Remark 4.24]; that remark was not read.

nodes.title: The retraction X^an → Σ(X, V) is continuous and the skeleton is connected
nodes.statement: For a semistable vertex set V, define τ_V: X^an → Σ(X, V) by sending x ∉ Σ to the unique limit-boundary point of its component (an open ball) in X^an ∖ Σ, and τ_V = id on Σ. Then τ_V is continuous, restricts on each generalized open annulus A of the decomposition to the retraction τ_A: A → Σ(A), and Σ(X, V) and Σ̂(X, V) are connected.
hypotheses: Continuity at points of V ('τ_V^{-1}(U) contains an open neighbourhood of x for x ∈ V') is left as an exercise in the source.
proofSteps: On annuli τ_V = τ_A is continuous by Lemma 2.12; at vertices the source leaves the check to the reader.
Proposition 3.9: the continuous image of the connected X^an under τ_V is Σ.
acceptance: The retraction of a point in an open-ball component of X^an ∖ Σ is the single point of its limit boundary, which lies in Σ but need not be a vertex of V: by Lemma 3.4(3) it is a point of Σ, and for a ball hanging off the interior of an edge it is an interior point of that edge. Compatibility of the retractions under refinement of V (subdividing an edge) is a reviewer-authored test; the refinement theory is Proposition 3.13, which was not read.

nodes.title: Existence of semistable vertex sets and characterization of minimal skeleta (statement)
nodes.statement: Theorem 4.22: a semistable vertex set of X exists. If V is a minimal semistable vertex set then (1) if χ(X) ≤ 0, Σ(X, V) is the set of points of X^an with no affinoid neighbourhood isomorphic to B(1); (2) if χ(X) < 0, V is stable and V = {x ∈ Σ(X, V): x is a topological vertex (valence ≥ 3) or g(x) > 0}. Corollary 4.23: for χ(X) ≤ 0 there is a unique set-theoretic minimal skeleton and for χ(X) < 0 a unique stable vertex set.
hypotheses: Existence is deduced from Deligne-Mumford's stable reduction theorem in the analytic form of Bosch-Lutkebohmert [BL85, Theorem 7.1] over a non-noetherian rank-1 valuation ring; the source's proof beyond its first lines was not read.

χ(X) is the Euler characteristic of Definition 4.19 and g(x) the genus of a type-2 point (Section 4, not read). A topological vertex means a vertex of valence at least 3, as defined just before Theorem 4.22.
proofSteps: Existence for X̂: the classical Deligne-Mumford theorem, in the analytic form proved over a non-noetherian rank-1 valuation ring in [BL85, Theorem 7.1].
Existence for the punctured X: "follows from Proposition 3.13(3)" (unread), not from an ad hoc addition of vertices separating punctures.

Minimality: for χ(X) < 0 the second assertion follows by applying Proposition 4.21 "in the standard way"; for χ(X) ≤ 0, Proposition 4.21(1) makes every genus-zero vertex of Σ have valence at least two, and Lemma 3.4(4) gives Σ′ ⊂ Σ for the set Σ′ of points without an affinoid neighbourhood isomorphic to B(1). Propositions 3.13 and 4.21 were not read; the rest of the proof of (1) was not read.
acceptance: A genus ≥ 2 curve has a unique stable vertex set; a Tate curve (χ = 0) has a unique minimal skeleton (the loop) but no unique minimal vertex set.

nodes.title: Faithful tropicalization of finite subgraphs and the tropical multiplicity formula (statements)
nodes.statement: Standing hypotheses (stated in the introduction): K is an algebraically closed field complete with respect to a nontrivial nonarchimedean valuation, and X is a nonsingular curve over K. H°(X^an) is the set of non-leaves of X^an, i.e. the points contained in an embedded open segment; the leaves are the K-points together with the type-4 points, so H°(X^an) is not simply the complement of the type-1 points. Its canonical metric is defined through semistable models ([BPR13]). (Theorem 1.1) For every finite embedded subgraph Γ ⊂ H°(X^an) there is a closed embedding of X into a quasiprojective toric variety, meeting the dense torus T, such that Γ maps isometrically onto its image in Trop(X ∩ T); the set of such embeddings is stable under domination and hence cofinal. (Theorem 1.3) Trop(X ∩ T) has a polyhedral structure such that for each edge e' finitely many segments e_1, ..., e_r of H°(X^an) map homeomorphically onto e', every other segment in the preimage is contracted, and the tropical multiplicity is m_Trop(e') = m_rel(e_1) + ... + m_rel(e_r), where m_rel(e) is the absolute value of the integer slope of the affine map e → e'. (Theorem 1.4) If in_w(X ∩ T) is irreducible and generically reduced for all w in a finite subgraph Γ' ⊂ Trop(X ∩ T), there is a unique embedded subgraph Γ ⊂ H°(X^an) mapping homeomorphically onto Γ', and this map is an isometry. For an affine curve embedded by invertible functions f_1, ..., f_n, m_rel(e) = gcd(s_1(e), ..., s_n(e)) with s_i(e) the absolute value of the slope of the integer-affine function log|f_i| along e (Remark 5.6; slopes computable by the slope formula of BPR13 Theorem 5.15).
hypotheses: K algebraically closed and complete with a nontrivial valuation; X nonsingular (both stated in the introduction). Trop(X ∩ T) is the closure of trop(X(K) ∩ T), with the polyhedral structure of Theorem 4.28 (not read).
Proofs (Sections 4-6: polyhedral domains, Theorem 4.30 finiteness of ψ^P, Theorem 5.8 compatibility of multiplicities, Corollary 5.9) were not read.
proofSteps: As described in the introduction: relate expansion factors m_rel(e) to tropical multiplicities through initial degenerations (Corollary 5.9); refine embeddings so that contracted edges or expansion factors > 1 are corrected; stability under domination gives cofinality (Section 5.15 domination order).
acceptance: For an elliptic curve with bad reduction the skeleton loop has length −val(j); a plane model that contracts the loop or has expansion factor > 1 is repaired by a refined embedding, recovering the Katz-Markwig-Markwig tropical j-invariant statements (Example 2.8, Section 6).
If an edge e' has tropical multiplicity 1, there is a unique segment e ⊂ H°(X^an) over it and its length equals the tropical length of e'.

review.notes:
Both sources are outside the library, so the reviewer re-fetched them from arXiv: the packet's SHA-256 values are correct for arXiv:1404.0279v1 and arXiv:1104.0320v3, the arXiv stamps match the recorded editions, and a pdftotext -layout extraction reproduces every cited line number. All four nodes and all three links were checked; all four nodes were corrected, none is unverifiable.
Corrections: (1) the standing conventions of the structure paper were garbled (X is the curve, X̂ its smooth completion, D = X̂ ∖ X); (2) H°(X^an) is the space of non-leaves, which excludes type-4 points as well as K-points; (3) the tropicalization paper does state its standing hypotheses in the introduction, contrary to the packet's note; (4) the existence of a semistable vertex set for a punctured curve follows from Proposition 3.13(3), not from an ad hoc vertex addition; (5) the retraction of a ball component lands in Σ but not necessarily in V; (6) slopes in the gcd formula are absolute values. Acceptance items that depend on unread sections are now labelled.
The three links have the right direction and their cited locations do use the source node's output; the reasons and locators were sharpened, in particular by recording that the tropicalization paper cites [BPR13] (the structure paper) for the metric on H°(X^an). Note for integration: the link from TB.2 to TB.5 is a stage-level edge that the atlas does not have (it routes TB.2 → TB.3 → TB.5); it is acyclic.
All parentStageIds are TB.2 or TB.5 and are owned by the roadmap; all eight coverage stage ids exist. A gap was added recording that neither paper is in CATALOGUE.json. Packet status stays partial.
